title: Minerals & Rock Formation
overview: Complete conceptual breakdown of minerals, Mohs hardness scale, rock cycle, and rock-forming mineral groups.

sections.title: Level 1: What is this topic? (Ye Topic Kya Hai?)
sections.content_text: Is topic me hum minerals aur rocks ke basic fundamentals samajhte hain. Mineral ek naturally occurring, inorganic solid substance hota hai jiska ek definite chemical composition aur ordered crystalline atomic structure hota hai. Rock do ya do se zyada minerals ka aggregate (mixture) hota hai. GATE Mining Engineering me har saal Mohs hardness scale, mineral identification, aur rock classification par direct factual aur conceptual questions aate hain.

sections.title: Level 2: Why does it matter? (GATE aur Mining me iska kya role hai?)
sections.content_text: Mining Engineers ke liye rock aur mineral properties samajhna sabse pehla step hai. Jab hum blasting karte hain, shaft sink karte hain, ya tunnels banate hain, to cutting speed, bit wear (drill bit ka ghisna), explosive energy consumption, aur roof stability sidhe mineralogy (jaise quartz content) aur rock type (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic) par depend karti hai. GATE exam me Mohs hardness sequence aur rock classification standard scoring questions hote hain.

sections.title: Level 3: Basic Concepts (Mool Bhoot Siddhant)
sections.content_text:
1. Rock Types:
- Igneous Rocks: Magma ya lava ke cooling aur solidification se banti hain (e.g., Granite, Basalt, Gabbro).
- Sedimentary Rocks: Pre-existing rocks ke weathering, deposition, compaction aur cementation se banti hain. Coal seams hamesha sedimentary rocks me paye jaate hain (e.g., Sandstone, Shale, Limestone).
- Metamorphic Rocks: High temperature aur pressure ke prabhav se existing rocks ka structure aur mineralogy change hone par banti hain (e.g., Quartzite, Marble, Gneiss).

2. Mohs Hardness Scale (Relative Scratch Hardness):
1: Talc (Softest)
2: Gypsum
3: Calcite
4: Fluorite
5: Apatite
6: Orthoclase Feldspar
7: Quartz
8: Topaz
9: Corundum
10: Diamond (Hardest)

Easy Memory Trick: 'The Girls Can Flirt And Other Queer Things Can Do' (T-G-C-F-A-O-Q-T-C-D).

sections.title: Level 4: Important Formulas & Relations (Zaroori Sutra)
sections.content_text:
1. Specific Gravity (G):
G = W_dry / (W_dry - W_submerged)
Variables: W_dry = Dry weight of rock specimen (N ya g), W_submerged = Specimen submerged in water weight (N ya g).
Unit: Dimensionless.

2. Mohs Hardness Test Rule: Harder mineral scratch karega softer mineral ko. Agar mineral A scratches mineral B, to Hardness(A) > Hardness(B).

3. Quartz Content & Abrasivity: Quartz abrasive index badhane me sabse bada factor hai. High quartz rock drill bit wear rate ko exponentially increase karta hai.

sections.title: Level 5: Simple Example (Aasan Udaharan)
sections.content_text:
Question: Ek mineral sample Calcite (Hardness 3) ko scratch kar sakta hai, lekin Apatite (Hardness 5) se scratch ho jaata hai. Fluorite (Hardness 4) ko ye sample scratch nahi kar pata balki Fluorite isko scratch kar deta hai. Sample ki Mohs hardness kiske barabar ya beech me hai?

Solution:
Calcite = 3, Fluorite = 4, Apatite = 5.
Since sample Calcite ko scratch karta hai => Hardness > 3.
Fluorite sample ko scratch karta hai => Hardness < 4.
Isliye sample ki Mohs hardness 3 aur 4 ke beech me hai (around 3.5).

sections.title: Level 6: GATE-Level Example (GATE Pattern Question)
sections.content_text:
Question (GATE Pattern):
Match the following rocks with their primary geological classification:
P: Basalt
Q: Sandstone
R: Gneiss
S: Granite

Options:
1. Extrusive Igneous
2. Intrusive Igneous
3. Clastic Sedimentary
4. Foliated Metamorphic

Explanation:
- Basalt surface par lava ke tezi se thande hone se banta hai => Extrusive Igneous (1)
- Sandstone sand grains ke compaction se banti hai => Clastic Sedimentary (3)
- Gneiss granite ya sedimentary rocks par intense metamorphism se banti hai jisme banding (foliation) hoti hai => Foliated Metamorphic (4)
- Granite zameen ke neeche magma ke slow cooling se banta hai => Intrusive Plutonic Igneous (2)
Correct Match: P-1, Q-3, R-4, S-2.

sections.title: Level 7: Previous Year GATE Questions Analysis (PYQ Analysis)
sections.content_text:
GATE MN me is topic se related standard questions:
- GATE 2020: Mohs hardness sequence par direct 1-mark question.
- GATE 2018: Diamond aur Corundum ke scratch behavior par numerical-linked concept.
Key Observation: GATE me hamesha order pucha jata hai (increasing ya decreasing). Question dhyan se padhna chahiye ki 'ascending' pucha hai ya 'descending'.

sections.title: Level 8: Quick Revision & Exam Checklist (Exam Day Checklist)
sections.content_text:
- Talc is the softest (Hardness 1), Diamond is the hardest (Hardness 10).
- Calcite ka cleavage rhombohedral hota hai.
- Coal sedimentary origin ka rock hai jisme carbonaceous matter rich hota hai.
- Sandstone reservoir rock aur roof rock dono ban sakti hai coal mines me.

title: Blast Design: Burden, Spacing, Powder Factor & PPV
overview: Master surface blast geometry, burden to spacing ratios, powder factor calculations, and ground vibration attenuation laws.

sections.title: Level 1: What is this topic? (Ye Topic Kya Hai?)
sections.content_text: Blast Design ka matlab hai opencast ya underground mines me rock fragmentation ke liye holes ka arrangement, explosive quantity, delay timing, aur vibration safety determine karna. Burden (free face se hole ki distance), spacing (do holes ke beech ki doori), bench height, aur sub-drilling iske core geometric parameters hain.

sections.title: Level 2: Why does it matter? (GATE aur Mining me iska kya role hai?)
sections.content_text: GATE Mining paper me Blast Design se har saal minimum 2 se 4 marks ke numericals aate hain! Powder factor calculate karna, blast vibration (Peak Particle Velocity - PPV) predict karna, flyrock prevent karna, aur shovel-dumper loading cost minimize karna ek Mining Engineer ka sabse important role hota hai.

sections.title: Level 3: Basic Concepts (Mool Bhoot Siddhant)
sections.content_text:
1. Burden (B): Hole aur nearest free face ke beech perpendicular distance.
2. Spacing (S): Same row me adjacent holes ke beech ki doori. Typically S = 1.15*B se 1.5*B hota hai.
3. Bench Height (H): Vertical height of the excavation step.
4. Stemming (T): Inactive drill hole collar length jo inert material (sand, drill cuttings) se fill ki jaati hai taaki explosive gas escape na ho.
5. Sub-drilling (J): Grade line ke neeche extra depth drill karna taaki toe na bache. Typically J = 0.2*B to 0.3*B.
6. Powder Factor (PF):
- Opencast Coal: m3 of rock broken per kg of explosive (m3/kg)
- Opencast Metal: Tonnes of ore broken per kg of explosive (t/kg).

sections.title: Level 4: Important Formulas & Variables (Zaroori Sutra)
sections.content_text:
1. Volume of Rock Broken per Hole (V):
V = B * S * H (in m3)
Variables: B = Burden (m), S = Spacing (m), H = Bench height (m).

2. Tonnage per Hole (M):
M = B * S * H * rho_rock (in tonnes)
rho_rock = In-situ rock density (tonnes/m3).

3. Powder Factor (PF):
PF = (Total Tonnes Broken) / (Total Explosive Consumed)  [t/kg]
Ya: PF = (Total m3 Broken) / (Total Explosive Consumed) [m3/kg]

4. USBM Ground Vibration Attenuation Law (PPV):
PPV = K * (D / sqrt(Q))^(-beta)
Variables:
PPV = Peak Particle Velocity (mm/s)
D = Distance from blast point to structure (m)
Q = Maximum instantaneous explosive charge per delay (kg)
(D / sqrt(Q)) = Scaled Distance (SD) in m/kg^0.5
K, beta = Site-specific rock transmission constants.

sections.title: Level 5: Simple Example (Aasan Udaharan)
sections.content_text:
Problem:
Ek open pit mine me:
Burden B = 4 m
Spacing S = 5 m
Bench height H = 10 m
Har hole me explosive charge = 80 kg.
Rock density = 2.5 tonnes/m3.
Powder factor (t/kg) calculate karein.

Solution:
Step 1: Volume broken per hole = B * S * H = 4 * 5 * 10 = 200 m3.
Step 2: Mass broken per hole = 200 * 2.5 = 500 tonnes.
Step 3: Powder Factor = 500 tonnes / 80 kg = 6.25 tonnes/kg.
Answer: 6.25 t/kg.

sections.title: Level 6: GATE-Level Example (GATE Pattern Question)
sections.content_text:
Question (GATE Pattern Numerical):
In a blast, the vibration attenuation relation is given by:
PPV = 1000 * (D / sqrt(Q))^(-1.6) mm/s.
A building is located at a distance D = 200 m from the blast site. The permissible PPV at the building is 10 mm/s. The maximum permissible explosive charge per delay Q (in kg) rounded off to 2 decimal places is:

Solution:
10 = 1000 * (200 / sqrt(Q))^(-1.6)
=> 10 / 1000 = (200 / sqrt(Q))^(-1.6)
=> 0.01 = (200 / sqrt(Q))^(-1.6)
Taking both sides to power (-1/1.6):
=> (0.01)^(-0.625) = 200 / sqrt(Q)
=> 0.01^(-0.625) = 17.7828
=> 200 / sqrt(Q) = 17.7828
=> sqrt(Q) = 200 / 17.7828 = 11.2468
=> Q = (11.2468)^2 = 126.49 kg.

Answer: 126.49 kg.

sections.title: Level 7: Previous Year GATE Questions Analysis (PYQ Analysis)
sections.content_text:
- GATE 2021 & 2023 dono me PPV equation aur Scaled Distance formula par direct 2-mark NAT question pucha gaya tha.
- Common Trap: Question me total explosive diya hota hai, lekin formula me 'Charge per Delay' (Q) use hota hai. Students aksar total charge rakh dete hain aur answer galat ho jaata hai!

sections.title: Level 8: Quick Revision & Exam Checklist
sections.content_text:
- S/B ratio usually 1.15 to 1.5 hota hai.
- Sub-drilling toe problem eliminate karne ke liye zaroori hoti hai.
- Scaled distance square-root scaling (D / sqrt(Q)) surface vibrations ke liye use hoti hai.
- Cylindrical charges ke liye cube-root scaling (D / Q^(1/3)) body waves ke liye use hoti hai.

title: Mine Airflow Dynamics: Atkinson Equation & Resistance
overview: Master fluid mechanics in underground airways, Atkinson's equation, airway resistance, series/parallel splits, and air power calculations.

sections.title: Level 1: What is this topic? (Ye Topic Kya Hai?)
sections.content_text: Mine Airflow Dynamics underground roadways me air ke flow, friction losses, aur ventilation pressure drops ko calculate karne ka science hai. Jab air khadaan ki rough walls, bends, aur galleries se guzarti hai, to friction aur turbulence ki wajah se pressure drop hota hai. Isko Atkinson's Equation se describe kiya jaata hai.

sections.title: Level 2: Why does it matter? (GATE aur Mining me iska kya role hai?)
sections.content_text: Mine Ventilation section GATE MN ka sabse heavy scoring numerical area hai! Atkinson's equation, airway resistance R, splits me air quantity distribution, aur ventilation fan motor power par har saal 4 se 6 marks ke direct questions aate hain.

sections.title: Level 3: Basic Concepts (Mool Bhoot Siddhant)
sections.content_text:
1. Atkinson's Law of Mine Ventilation:
Ventilation pressure drop (P) airway ke friction factor, rubbing surface area, aur square of air velocity ke directly proportional hota hai.

2. Square Law of Airflow:
P = R * Q^2
Jahan P = Pressure drop (Pa), R = Airway Resistance (Ns^2/m^8 ya kg/m^7), Q = Airflow quantity (m3/s).

3. Resistance Relations:
- Series Airway: Total Resistance R_total = R1 + R2 + R3 + ...
- Parallel Airway: 1 / sqrt(R_total) = 1 / sqrt(R1) + 1 / sqrt(R2) + ...

4. Equivalent Orifice (Murgue's Formula):
A_eq = 0.385 / sqrt(R)  [in m2, for standard air density 1.2 kg/m3].

sections.title: Level 4: Important Formulas & Variables (Zaroori Sutra)
sections.content_text:
1. Atkinson's Equation:
P = (k * S * Q^2) / A^3
Variables:
P = Frictional pressure loss (Pa or N/m2)
k = Friction factor of roadway (kg/m3 ya Ns^2/m^4)
S = Rubbing surface area = Periphery (O) * Length (L) = O * L (m2)
A = Cross-sectional area of roadway (m2)
Q = Air quantity (m3/s).

2. Airway Resistance (R):
R = (k * S) / A^3 = (k * O * L) / A^3
Note: Agar cross-sectional area double ho jaye to resistance (1/2)^3 = 1/8th ho jaata hai!

3. Air Power Consumed (P_air):
P_air = (P * Q) Watts = (P * Q) / 1000 kW

4. Fan Shaft Power / Motor Power:
Motor Power = P_air / (eta_fan * eta_motor) kW.

sections.title: Level 5: Simple Example (Aasan Udaharan)
sections.content_text:
Problem:
Ek mine roadway me 40 m3/s hawa flow ho rahi hai aur pressure drop 640 Pa hai. Roadway ka resistance (R) calculate karein.

Solution:
Formula: P = R * Q^2
=> R = P / Q^2
=> R = 640 / (40)^2 = 640 / 1600 = 0.4 Ns^2/m^8.
Answer: R = 0.4 Ns^2/m^8.

sections.title: Level 6: GATE-Level Example (GATE Pattern Question)
sections.content_text:
Question (GATE 2022 Pattern):
A circular airway of diameter 4 m and length 500 m has a friction factor k = 0.01 Ns^2/m^4. If the air quantity flowing through the airway is 50 m3/s, calculate:
(a) Airway resistance R
(b) Pressure loss P
(c) Air power in kW.

Solution:
Step 1: Area A = pi * r^2 = pi * (2)^2 = 4*pi = 12.566 m2.
Perimeter O = pi * d = 4*pi = 12.566 m.
Rubbing surface S = O * L = 12.566 * 500 = 6283.18 m2.

Step 2: Resistance R = (k * S) / A^3
=> R = (0.01 * 6283.18) / (12.566)^3 = 62.8318 / 1984.34 = 0.03166 Ns^2/m^8.

Step 3: Pressure drop P = R * Q^2
=> P = 0.03166 * (50)^2 = 0.03166 * 2500 = 79.16 Pa.

Step 4: Air Power = (P * Q) / 1000 = (79.16 * 50) / 1000 = 3.96 kW.

Answer: R = 0.0317 Ns^2/m^8, P = 79.16 Pa, Power = 3.96 kW.

sections.title: Level 7: Previous Year GATE Questions Analysis (PYQ Analysis)
sections.content_text:
- GATE 2020, 2021, 2023 me parallel airways ke split flow ratio par questions the. Parallel airways me P dono branch me same hota hai: P = R1 * Q1^2 = R2 * Q2^2 => Q1 / Q2 = sqrt(R2 / R1).
- Common Trap: Students k ko density ya kinematic viscosity se confuse kar lete hain. Atkinson formula me k empirical friction factor hai.

sections.title: Level 8: Quick Revision & Exam Checklist
sections.content_text:
- P = R * Q^2.
- Air power = (P * Q) / 1000 kW.
- Parallel airways me Q proportional to 1 / sqrt(R).
- Series airways me R_total = R1 + R2.
- Equivalent orifice A = 0.385 / sqrt(R).
